summary: Iteration 20 verification of resumable page-explain background job + admin-only Regenerate button on the client trust preview + supervisord.conf. All backend and frontend checks pass. The RESUME branch (not the failed-fallback branch) fired during the mid-run restart test.
critical_code_review_comments: page_explanation_jobs.start_page_explain_job correctly guards against duplicate work via _jobs status check, but note _jobs is per-process — with `--workers 2` in the new supervisord.conf two workers could each accept a regenerate call and race on the same case. sweep_stuck_jobs_on_startup only runs on boot, so mid-run duplication between workers is possible. Consider adding a MongoDB-level lock (unique index on {case_id, status:'pending'}) or route the regenerate endpoint through a single worker via sticky session.

server.py _resume_page_job closure uses a walrus assignment inside a kwarg (`admin_id=(job_admin := (case.get('trust_page_job') or {}).get('admin_id') or 'system')`) — the walrus var `job_admin` is never referenced afterwards, so it can be simplified to a plain expression. Minor readability nit.

Client-facing GET /trust-cases/{id}/trust-page-explanations exposes the raw `error` field from the job (e.g., 'Server restarted mid-run…'). That's helpful for admins but potentially confusing wording for end clients — consider suppressing/rephrasing for role=='client'.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env — set it in env before pytest (`export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=...`). Empirically the run finishes in ~30s not 45s, so restart earlier than 15s if you want to catch mid-run.
